newsitem.title: USA: Hoffa reviewing "discrepancy" in Teamster vote.
newsitem.headline: Hoffa reviewing "discrepancy" in Teamster vote.

text.p: The apparently unsuccessful campaign of James Hoffa for president of the Teamsters Union said Monday it is reviewing a "discrepancy" in ballot-counting that gave incumbent union President Ron Carey a narrow lead.

After all eligible votes were tallied late Saturday, court-appointed Election Officer Barbara Zack Quindel accounted for 485,605 ballots returned, including 41,002 uncounted ballots that are being checked for eligibility this week.
But last week she reported that the total number of mail-in ballots received was 511,268, an estimate based on receipts from the U.S. Postal Service.

"There appears to be a massive discrepancy between the amount of ballots counted and the amount of ballots received," said Hoffa spokesman Richard Leebove. "It's inexplicable. We are continuing to review her figures."

Hoffa, 55, son and namesake of the late Jimmy Hoffa, who ruled the union in the 1950s and 1960s, sought to unseat Carey, 60, who was elected president of the 1.4 million-member International Brotherhood of Teamsters as a reformer in 1991.

Leebove said the campaign was considering asking Attorney General Janet Reno to impound the ballots and asking Congress to investigate the election, which is governed by a 1989 consent decree that settled a federal anti-racketeering suit.

"Unless she can account for 25,000 ballots I think this goes to our original protest that was filed on Wednesday," he said, referring to a complaint the Hoffa campaign lodged with Quindel that alleged four procedural irregularities.

Leebove said the Hoffa campaign believed the Postal Service receipts were based on automated tabulations of bar-codes on the business reply envelopes. But Quindel spokesman Jeff O'Mara and Carey campaign aide Bob Hauptman said they believe the postal receipts were based on a less accurate estimate of the weight of the envelopes.

Hauptman said observers from both campaigns who witnessed the trays of returned ballots being loaded by the election officer's staff agreed on an estimate of about 486,000 ballots, based on an assumption of 400 ballots per tray.
"Personally, I have a lot more faith in that estimate than what the Post Office charges," Hauptman said.

Carey spokeswoman Renee Asher dismissed the discrepancy claim and noted that both campaigns had observers at every phase of the ballot-collection and counting process. "It just doesn't make sense," she said. "The bottom line is that they lost and they're whining."

The election officer reported 226,593 votes for Carey and 209,896 for Hoffa out of a total of 441,797 counted. An additional 2,806 ballots were declared void because election procedures were not followed.
The additional 41,002 ballots that were set aside for eligibility checks are being processed this week. Carey's re-election will not be official until they are processed.
If his victory margin should fall to within 3 percentage points, a recount is required under the election rules.
